A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACCO and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The retained algorithm and experiments can be matched reliably despite rewriting, renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original communication measurements, language-model pretraining and fine-tuning results, and simulated heterogeneous-worker experiments in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a DPU batch-size ablation in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The two-stage accumulation mechanism, delay compensation, optimizer sharding and parallel streams are retained. Algorithm 1 is identical apart from pagination. v2 explicitly simplifies the main exposition to fixed batch sizes while retaining time-varying accumulation in the appendix.

E1.justification: TinyStories, OpenWebText, LAMBADA evaluation, Alpaca fine-tuning and the communication-timing scenario are retained. The simulated slow-worker experiment moves from v1 Appendix C to v2 Section 4.6; it is not new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds analytical memory/capability comparisons for DiLoCo, DPU and WP, reporting 150 GB, 46 GB and 46 GB respectively under its stated assumptions. Empirical training comparators remain unchanged: WP is renamed from ACCO-wp, and no DiLoCo training experiment is reported.

E3.justification: The new Appendix A.1 control compares DPU with 40 warmup steps using one versus two accumulation steps, halving the effective batch size and doubling optimizer updates per minibatch. The retained main experiments and hyperparameter Tables 4–5 keep their earlier settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a batch-size sensitivity analysis testing whether more frequent DPU updates improve convergence. Existing warmup, weight-prediction and slow-worker analyses remain. The two-node fine-tuning loss-versus-minibatches panel from v1 Figure 11 is removed, while the single-node panel remains.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averaging for the TinyStories delayed-update curves. No additional run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are supplied. v2's checklist calls large-scale runs deterministic without adding replication or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Perplexities in Table 2 and training times in Table 3 are unchanged. New Figure 10 reports faster early convergence but worse final loss for half-batch DPU. The two-node minibatch-based validation results are removed, and the slow-worker discussion corrects the idle-time fraction from one-third to three-quarters.

T1.justification: v1 provides algorithmic equations without convergence theorems. v2 introduces GD and bounded-variance SGD convergence propositions, smoothness and unbiasedness assumptions, a Lyapunov function, and extensive proofs in Appendix A.2. This adds a substantial formal component.

C1.justification: v2 introduces standard SGD convergence-rate guarantees as an explicit contribution in the introduction and conclusion, extending v1's empirical convergence claims. The central claims about sharding, warmup-free compensation and wall-clock acceleration remain.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 6's hardware-bias, communication/energy and further-memory-saving limitations, along with the explanation of early fine-tuning data inefficiency. It newly links AdamW training alignment to SGD theory. Its checklist briefly adds failure/delay boundaries and possible energy-efficiency benefits, rather than retaining the earlier qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 changes the stated code repository and adds a SLURM/configuration listing in Appendix B.3. However, its learning rate of 1e-5 and ACCO accumulation count of 4 conflict with Table 5's 2e-5 and 2. These are additional, inconsistent disclosures rather than established changes to the reported runs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion covering DiLoCo, DiLoCo scaling, PETRA, DeepSpeed and delayed-SGD analysis, while pruning decentralized communication-acceleration literature. The principal positioning against local-update methods and alongside sharded training remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition are substantially rewritten. Empirical motivation is folded into the experiments section, the heterogeneous-worker study moves into the main text, and appendices are reorganized. The title changes, ACCO-wp becomes WP, and a checklist is added.

P2.justification: Most diagrams and plots are retained. Display changes include a redesigned, expanded and color-coded Table 1, a compacted Table 3, relocated figures, the new ablation plot and removal of one fine-tuning panel. The added configuration listing is split across pages 23 and 25.

improvement.justification: The new batch-size ablation adds useful evidence, and the convergence analysis could substantially strengthen the rationale. However, Appendix A.2's SGD distance-update expansion conflicts with its stated recurrences, the new configuration contradicts Table 5, and substantive limitations and data-efficiency qualifications disappear. With principal empirical results unchanged and the central added proof internally inconsistent, these benefits and reliability losses do not support a confident net quality judgment.
